questions.asked: Can the panel runtime read its own document computed style, in a browser?
questions.statement: It can. In the panel own chrome-extension:// document, in Chrome 159.0.8154.13, getComputedStyle returned all six declared properties for all four baseline hooks in both colour schemes, and document.styleSheets exposed the panel own baseline sheet with its 16 rules and their declared values. Two further findings came with it: with the artefact at head the declarations apply (L4), while a fresh build at this head leaves the sheet behind media="print" that the document refuses to ungate (L5), so the same four hooks then read the browser defaults.

questions.asked: Which properties does the measurement declare, and which side declares each?
questions.answer: six: padding, borderTopWidth, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, fontFamily
questions.statement: The list is declared from the hooks the baseline names, not from what looked interesting: five properties are declared by a rule that names one of the four hooks (padding, borderTopWidth, backgroundColor, color, fontSize), and fontFamily is declared on body and inherited by every hook, included because the injected default has to be stated and marked not a discriminator.

questions.asked: Does the relay carry a style read, and does the own-document read need one?
questions.statement: The relay carries no style read today: the six relayed types are page events, the only two panel-to-page types are the replay request and the picker command, the isolated-world listener answers only those two, and no style reading appears at any hop. The panel own-document read needs no relay leg: it is a getComputedStyle call in the panel own document, measured here without one.

relayRuling.ruling: The relay carries no style read today. The panel own-document read needs no relay leg. No relay leg is built in this milestone.
because: R1, R2 and R3 name every type that crosses a hop, and none of them names a property, an element or a computed value (R6).
R5 shows the isolated-world listener answers only the replay request and the picker command and returns false for anything else, so a style request would be answered by nothing at all.

R7 shows getComputedStyle has no call site in the panel source or the extension scripts, and R8 to R10 show the panel reaches no page by eval, by executeScript or by any other use of the scripting permission.

L2 and L3 measure the own-document read succeeding with no message, no relay and no inspectedWindow reach, which is why a relay leg would serve only a picked inspected-page host, and C2 rules that out.

claims.statement: The background re-broadcasts exactly six page message types: angular-ai:record, state, di-graph, error-capture, picker-state and picked.

The first of the two panel-to-page routes is the replay request (extension/background.js:42-84): the panel sends angular-ai:state-request naming a tab, the tab id is validated, and the background forwards { type: angular-ai:replay-request } into that tab and re-emits the answer as angular-ai:state and angular-detected.

The second of the two panel-to-page routes is the picker command (extension/background.js:89-125): tab id and action (arm or cancel) are validated, and { type: angular-ai:picker-command, action } is forwarded into the named tab.
The isolated-world relay forwards exactly the six page events, one runtime message each, and reads no payload beyond passing it on.
The isolated-world listener answers only angular-ai:replay-request and angular-ai:picker-command, and returns false for every other type so the rest of the extension may answer it.

No message type in that chain carries a style read: the six relayed types are page events, and the only two types that cross from the panel into a page are the replay request and the picker command, neither of which names a property, an element or a computed value.
getComputedStyle has zero call sites in the panel source and the extension scripts: the scan finds eight occurrences and every one of them is a comment line that states the absence.

claims.statement: With the artefact at head (extension/panel/index.html:9 links styles.css with no media condition), the baseline applies: every value the sheet declares for a hook is what that hook computes, and the only differences between the two sides are borderTopWidth, which the browser serialises as the device-pixel-snapped used value (2px reads 1.71429px and 1px reads 0.571429px at the measured devicePixelRatio 1.75), p.state, whose rule declares border-left at styles.css:65 and no border-top so its borderTopWidth reads 0px on both sides, and the colour p.state inherits from the section finding rule rather than declaring itself. claims.statement: A fresh build at this head emits the same sheet behind media="print" with an inline onload handler, and the panel document refuses that handler: the link parses as <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css" media="print" onload="this.media='all'">, document.styleSheets reports that sheet with media "print" (not disabled, 16 readable rules), and the page log records "Executing inline event handler violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'script-src 'self'' ... notClaimed: One instance (chrome-beta-nano, Chrome/159.0.8154.13) and one page (the Insurance Portal at route /home); nothing here says another browser version, another profile or another page reads the same.
One panel route (the lint demo surface) was measured; no other panel route or surface was read.
No inspected-page element was measured and nothing was read out of the portal document beyond its URL, title and ng-version: the reading is the panel own document, per C3.

No relay message was sent, and no message type, eval call or injection was added to the extension: this task builds nothing, and acceptance criterion 4 records that as a property of the tree rather than of this prose.
The visual-qa surface does not exist yet (T003 builds it): nothing here is a reading of it, and no property row was rendered.

The jsdom readings of scripts/panel-styles.test.mjs are not restated as a browser measurement; that suite is cited for what it proves, and its injected font-family observation is recorded as a cited record this task did not witness (M1).
The media="print" defect of the fresh build is recorded, not fixed, and not claimed to be the only thing between the panel document and its baseline: only the sheet media was measured as the gate.

The dark-scheme readings were taken through cdp Emulation.setEmulatedMedia, not under a dark operating-system setting; they say what the stylesheet resolves to under the query, not what a dark-theme user sees in every respect.
Nothing is claimed about the panel rendering correctly, about its appearance, or about whether the design is any good: this is a reading, not a judgement.
The light and dark readings agree across two runs of the same expression, which is repeatability within one instance, not a second observer.
unknowns: Why the injected root font family is "Times New Roman" in this instance while M039 recorded "Segoe UI" (panel-styles.test.mjs:15) was not measured: the profile standard-font setting, the --lang=da launch and the Chrome version all changed since that pass, and none of them was isolated here.

Whether the fresh build media="print" gate exists on a checkout whose toolchain differs from this one was not measured; what was measured is one fresh build at this head, and the artefact at head was emitted before it.
Whether every panel route reaches the same four hooks was not measured: the lint demo surface was the one route the reading ran on, and it renders the shared panel-demo markup.

The borderTopWidth serialisation was explained by the devicePixelRatio 1.75 that was measured, but the exact snapping rule Chrome applied (1px to 0.571429px, 2px to 1.71429px) is arithmetic consistent with the readings rather than a specification this task read.

The DevTools panel frame was driven by routing its own document with history.pushState and a popstate event, the way M039 measured the panel; whether a user clicking through the panel reaches the same document state was not measured.

The instrument itself (the raw CDP harness) lived in a session scratchpad and is not shipped, so the live half is pinned by its recorded answer and its verbatim expressions rather than by a re-runnable command in this tree.
